  ESTIMATE, not a measurement: what sending no_tools, notification, suggestion to a shared haiku tier would have cost, over the tokens actually recorded.
  A call is warm only when the previous routable side call of the same conversation was inside the cache TTL; nothing else would keep that tier warm. Cold calls pay a full write of the whole prompt.
  A call whose prompt exceeds haiku's 150,000-token ceiling cannot be routed there at all and is counted under "over ceiling", never in the saving.
  Both columns are priced at the same TTL per request (the one the record's extended-cache-ttl beta implies); no record in range logged it, so 5m was assumed throughout.
    side kind     routable  warm  cold  over ceiling   tokens  cache read  gap p50  $ at requested  $ at haiku   $ saved
    suggestion           3     2     1             -  185,135       98.8%     60 s         $0.1071     $0.0911   $0.0160
    notification         2     1     1             -  134,084       99.2%     20 s         $0.0766     $0.0963  $-0.0196
    no_tools             1     1     0             -    6,130       32.6%     10 s         $0.0224     $0.0008   $0.0216
    total                6     4     2             -  325,349                              $0.2061     $0.1881   $0.0180
  amortisation (break-even 3.1 warm calls per cold write; applies to kinds above 80.0% cache read, whose cost is the cached prefix):
    suggestion: 2.0 warm per cold - BELOW break-even, saves $0.0160
    notification: 1.0 warm per cold - BELOW break-even, COSTS $0.0196
    no_tools: 32.6% cache read - little prefix to lose, the rule does not apply; saves $0.0216
  simulated net over all routable kinds: saves $0.0180 - gross, before the exposure below.

  exposure: only a conversation pinned below the requested tier can lose the free warm cache its side calls provide today (they would no longer bill the requested model).
  conversations ever pinned below requested: 1 of 2
